item.text: {"winner":"B","confidence":"high","summary":"B is materially more mergeable because it verifies the core upload and retry behavior much more thoroughly, although both patches violate the explicit requirement to route Upload through FilesService.Add.","reasons":["B’s multipart test verifies the field, filename, and actual content; A never checks uploaded content.","B directly tests FilesService.Upload across a 429 and confirms the multipart content survives replay, while A only tests the retry transport with a generic bytes.Reader.","B provides distinct validation errors for an empty filename and nil content, whereas A combines them into a less informative error.","B documents the new convenience API and the replayability limitation of Add, improving usability and reviewability."],"risks_a":["Upload duplicates Add’s option handling, request construction, decoding, and error handling instead of calling Add, contrary to the frozen contract.","Tests omit Upload-level retry, uploaded content, validation, and source-reader failure coverage.","The generic bytes.Reader transport test does not establish that multipartbody.NewFile and Upload produce a replayable request end to end."],"risks_b":["Upload still duplicates Add rather than routing the encoded body through it, creating maintenance drift and violating an explicit contract requirement.","No tests cover empty-filename validation, nil-content validation, or propagation of source-reader errors.","The additional non-replayable Add test and extensive documentation are useful but somewhat broader than the minimum requested scope."]}
